tts_summary:
Good morning. Here's your Monday September 21st morning game plan.

Macro picture first. US futures are rallying despite a weekend that was almost entirely negative for risk sentiment. S&P futures are up about 65 basis points, Nasdaq up 110 basis points, and the Russell up roughly 47 basis points. Asia closed broadly higher — Korea up 1.65%, Hang Seng up 1.18%, mainland China up about 1 percent. Europe is up 85 to 120 basis points with data center infrastructure names leading. Treasuries have a modest bid, yields down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve.

So what's driving the strength? In a word — diplomacy. The UN General Assembly runs in New York from Monday through September 28th, and markets are betting that face-to-face meetings between leaders could cool tensions in the Middle East. Trump has signaled openness to meeting Iran's president, who is expected to attend. That matters enormously because nearly every macro problem markets are dealing with right now — elevated yields, inflation pressure, margin compression, weak consumer confidence — traces back to oil. Brent is sitting around $102 a barrel and sliding this morning, down about 170 basis points. Even a modest de-escalation in the Iran conflict could trigger an outsized drop in energy prices and unlock a cascade of positive macro effects.

But here's the tension. The weekend news was genuinely bad. Houthis dramatically escalated missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, targeting Riyadh's airport fuel depot. Ukraine launched its largest drone strike of the war on Russia, hitting a Moscow-area oil refinery. Trump nearly authorized air strikes against the Houthis Sunday night before backing off at the last minute. Motor oil is being rationed at US retailers. Tanker costs are surging. The Fed remains hawkish — the market is pricing roughly 33 basis points more in hikes over the final two meetings of the year, with Kansas City Fed President Schmid and Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari both warning over the weekend that inflation is running hot beyond just energy.

On the AI and tech side, there was a flood of negative headlines after Friday's close. Anthropic's IPO has been delayed, its 2027 annual recurring revenue projections disappointed, and OpenAI is projecting negative free cash flow of roughly $280 billion from 2026 through 2030. Oracle is also in focus — a Financial Times report flagged that efforts to offload debt tied to its massive New Mexico data center, called Project Jupiter, have hit a wall. Despite all of this, data center infrastructure names are holding up in Europe this morning.

On individual names: Novo Nordisk is underperforming after failing to give investors granular financial targets at its analyst day — shares sliding in Europe. Disney's parks business is bucking industry trends with traffic holding up thanks to price promotions and package deals — a relative bright spot. Paramount is in advanced settlement talks with California's attorney general over its Warner Bros Discovery merger, potentially requiring Comedy Central divestitures and CNN editorial independence commitments — outcome still uncertain.

Looking ahead this week, the Trump-Xi summit Thursday is the next major catalyst after the UN General Assembly. Expect modest tariff reductions on roughly $30 billion in goods and potentially a deal eliminating Chinese tariffs on American liquefied natural gas. US flash PMIs hit Wednesday morning. Meta Connect keynote from Zuckerberg is Wednesday night at 7pm Eastern. Key earnings this week include AutoZone Tuesday, Cintas, General Mills, and Paychex Wednesday, Darden and Costco Thursday.

Bottom line: the rally today is fragile and entirely dependent on geopolitical optionality. If the UN General Assembly produces even a hint of diplomatic progress on Iran, oil drops and the market can run. If it's a dud, the weight of the negative macro fundamentals reasserts itself quickly. Trade accordingly.
